prerequisites: Basic knowledge in design theory, technical drawing, and CAD.
Ability to solve applied problems in mechanical engineering designs.

Completion of the courses Mechanics 1, Technical Drawing/CAD, Fundamentals of Design Theory, and Technical Drawing/CAD Design Exercise is required to claim full participation in the Machine Elements Design Exercise.
Positive completion of StEOP is also mandatory.

learning_outcomes.text: Be able to independently design, calculate, and implement selected machine elements in constructions based on standards and calculation regulations.
Be able to independently solve design and construction tasks professionally.
Be able to recognize and apply the advantages and disadvantages of machine elements and their industrially relevant application areas in the constructive environment.
Be able to plan selected machine elements based on standards and calculation regulations.
Be able to process questions from the field of mechanical engineering constructions.
Be able to discuss the advantages and disadvantages of machine elements and their application areas in the constructive environment.
Be able to plan an independent construction in CAD.
Be able to analyze an independent construction in CAD.
Be able to describe the calculation and design of axles and shafts, rolling bearings, plain bearings, and lubrication.
Be able to select the design of axles and shafts, rolling bearings, plain bearings, and lubrication.
Be able to carry out the design of seals, shaft-hub connections, clutches, and brakes.
Be able to calculate gearings, spur and bevel gear drives, and belt drives.
Be able to carry out cross-disciplinary constructions with the content listed above.
Be able to plan an independent CAD construction and present it appropriately to the target audience.
Be able to explain one's own calculation method in calculation examples in one's own words.
Be able to analyze quality requirements for calculations.
Be able to investigate deviations and identify potential for improvement.
Be able to critically discuss own calculations within the framework of peer feedback.
Be able to plan learning and examination strategies and present results.

syllabus_topics: Calculation and design of axles and shafts
Gears, spur and bevel gear drives
Cross-disciplinary construction with the above-mentioned contents
teaching_methods: Lectures on theoretical foundations and basic tools of the mentioned contents
Practicing and applying content through presented calculation examples
Preparation of an independent construction with CAD

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment for independent CAD construction
